body:
Here is my analysis of the root cause:

1. When the value type of a typed Dictionary is explicitly declared as `Variant`,
   `GDScriptAnalyzer::resolve_datatype()` does not execute
   `result.set_container_element_type(1, value_type)`
   because of `if (value_type.kind != Variant)`,
   so the value slot is dropped during parsing,
   and `Dictionary[int, Variant]` is internally degraded to `Dictionary[int]`.
2. Consequently, when `GDScriptAnalyzer::resolve_return()` calls
   `check_type_compatibility()`, the source is missing the value slot,
   `p_source.has_container_element_type(1)` is `false`,
   the value type comparison (Variant vs String) never happens,
   and the return value is incorrectly accepted.
3. The function return path relies on `p_return->use_conversion == true`
   to generate `OPCODE_RETURN_TYPED_DICTIONARY` as a runtime safety net,
   but here it is not set, so only a plain `OPCODE_RETURN` is generated,
   there is no runtime type check, and the wrong static `String` type
   keeps propagating. At runtime the actual value is `int` (returned by `a()`),
   yet `bigrams()` is called as if it were a `String`,
   which may lead to a crash.

Note that for a regular assignment (such as `b = a`),
`write_assign()` forces `OPCODE_ASSIGN_TYPED_DICTIONARY`
as long as the target variable is a fully typed Dictionary,
and the runtime check intercepts the type mismatch.


The function return path generates that check only when `p_use_conversion == true`.
In this case, because the value slot information is missing,
neither fallback (static check nor runtime check) is triggered,
so the wrong static `String` type propagates to the caller.

This is my analysis; I am not sure whether it is correct,
and I am not able to fix it on my own.
If the analysis is correct, the most suspicious fix point is
the logic in `resolve_datatype()` that treats the value type as "non-existent".
but editing it may also affect all paths that go through `resolve_datatype()`,
such as function parameters, variable declarations, and casts.
